title: Diabetes emergencies in the hospital: DKA, HHS and hypoglycemia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's diabetes (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Hypoglycemic coma

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 76, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F.

Review of Systems:
Neurological: Positive (Unresponsive on arrival)
Endocrine: Positive (T2DM)
Cardiovascular: Negative
Respiratory: Negative
Gastrointestinal: Negative

History of Present Illness:
[Copied Forward from 04/10/2026]: Patient is a 77-year-old female with a history of T2DM. She reports stable glucose management on a sulfonylurea regimen. She denies any recent changes in diet or exercise.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted in a state of hypoglycemi and was found in a coma. She was immediately stabilized with a bolus of IV dextrose. Following the administration of intravenous fluids, she regained consciousness. She remained stable throughout the remainder of her stay. Her glucose levels were monitored closely, and her sulfonylurea dosage was adjusted to prevent future episodes. She was discharged once she was ambulatory and able to tolerate oral intake.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Hypoglycemi
2. Type 2 diabetes

Discharge Medications:
1. Metformin 500mg BID
2. Glipizide 5mg daily (dose reduced)

Follow-up:
Follow-up with primary care physician in 7 days for glucose monitoring.

Electronically signed,
R. Mensah, MD
05/15/2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes with hypoglycemia with coma: E11.641 (HCC 36).
